text:
The hum intensified, no longer a mere vibration but a low groan from the very stones of the courthouse. The microfilm reader's light flickered, then died, plunging the small corner of the archives into deeper shadow. Just as the last of the light faded, a hairline crack, thin as a spider's silk, snaked its way up the plaster wall beside him, tracing an almost perfect vertical line through the faded portrait of some long-dead mayor. It was a fresh wound, bleeding dust, a physical manifestation of the stress bleeding through Blackwood Bay's foundations, mirroring the financial rot Elias Thorne had so meticulously documented.

David pulled out his phone, a useless reflex. No signal. Not even the emergency channels. The digital maw had swallowed Blackwood Bay whole, leaving only the hum, now a throbbing pulse in his temples. He flipped open his waterproof notebook, a faint tremor running through his fingers, and his eyes caught the timestamp on the last police report he’d copied, a string of digits blurring: '07:63:7.56'. It was an impossible time, a numerical stutter in the fabric of reality, another seven-infused fragment whispering of a hidden ledger, a debt still being tallied, echoing the impossible figures Thorne kept writing into the town’s silent, unspoken contracts.
